title: PF2e outcome trace
description: The payload of a `pf2e.outcome` observation (RUL-13), which the PF2e system adapter `secondchair-foundry-pf2e` emits in every mode of play for each outcome it sees: a check roll, a damage roll, damage taken, a spell cast, a condition change, and the follow-up of an agent's system action (RUL-10). Each section is present only when the outcome has it. The PF2e System extension's rules checks read nothing else (RUL-14, RUL-15). Protocol version 0.1.0.

conditions.description: Condition slug -> its value, null for a condition with none.

type.description: pf2e's context type (attack-roll, saving-throw, skill-check, damage-roll, damage-taken, spell-cast, …), `condition` for a condition change, or `follow-up` for the condition an agent's system action gives its target.

message.description: The chat message's id, null for a condition change.

user.description: The Foundry user whose client made it (RUL-17).

actor.description: The rolling, casting or affected actor's UUID.

target.description: The targeted actor's UUID, if any.

action.description: The activity rolled, from pf2e's `action:<slug>` roll option (demoralize, trip, …).

roll.description: A check's roll and its breakdown.

natural.description: The d20 kept, null for a roll without one.

degree.description: The degree pf2e recorded, after adjustment.

damage.description: Damage taken: the damage roll applied, before IWR.

iwr.description: Damage taken: the immunities, weaknesses, resistances and hardness pf2e applied, as its damage-taken message shows them.

hp.description: Damage taken: the actor's HP and temporary HP before and after.

shield.description: Damage taken: the damage a blocking shield took, null when none blocked.

resource.description: A spell cast: what it spends, counted before and after (a spontaneous slot's uses, prepared copies not expended, focus points, innate uses); `none` for a cantrip or a free cast.

conditions.description: A condition change: the actor's conditions before (absent when the adapter had not seen them yet) and after.

follow_up.description: A follow-up (RUL-10): the condition the executor's system action gives its target at its degree, its value on the target before the call and once it settled (each absent when the target did not have it), and what the executor did: `applied` it, found it `already` applied, or left it `ambiguous` (changed while the call settled, not as the degree says), a discrepancy, never applied.

flags.description: Evidence for the trace readers (RUL-19), as the modules wrote it: `pf2e` ({dosAdjustments}), and when active `pf2e-toolbelt` (the message's), `pf2e-visioner` (the actor's token's), `pf2e-reaction` and `pf2e-combater` (its combatant's), `sundry` ({effects: the actor's effect slugs}).
